Show an ongoing notification so the system is less likely to stop DetoxDroid in the background.
Stops the system from putting DetoxDroid to sleep. Recommended if your phone aggressively closes background apps.
Some phones stop background apps to save battery, which can silently switch DetoxDroid off. These optional settings help it keep running.
DetoxDroid helps you spend less time stuck to your phone.
Uninstalling may fail because DetoxDroid has elevated permissions. Tap here to revoke them first.

This revokes DetoxDroid permissions so you can uninstall it normally.\n\nIf you install DetoxDroid again, you will need to grant these permissions again.
Grayscale is set up and waiting on one permission.
Scroll breaks and app blocking are waiting for the \"display over other apps\" permission.
Your phone may stop DetoxDroid in the background. Allow it to run without battery restrictions so your rules keep working.
Active in all apps except %d selected.
Example: select YouTube to exclude it.
Example: select YouTube to include only it.
Copies another feature\'s app selection over this one. The current selection is gone.
The feature is active all the time.
Limit this feature to specific days and time ranges.
No rules yet.\n\nThis feature is active all the time.
Automatically turns Do Not Disturb on while DetoxDroid is active. Configure exceptions in system settings.
Open Android settings to fine-tune Do Not Disturb.
Takes the color out of distracting apps. Where the system grayscale filter is out of reach, a screen filter dulls and blurs them instead.
Dims the screen below its normal minimum while a listed app is open. (Long-press to adjust intensity.)
Ignores temporary overlays (for example volume panel or status bar) so they do not change color mode.
Switch on grayscale, extra dim or the screen filter first.
Switch on the screen filter first, or set up real grayscale.
Switches the system color filter to grayscale while a listed app is open. Costs nothing in battery.
Real grayscale needs a one-time setup from a computer or via Shizuku. Until then, a filter washes the color out and blurs distracting apps.
Runs on top of the system grayscale filter. You already have the real thing, so this is only worth it if grayscale alone is too easy to ignore.
How far it goes. Stronger settings make text harder to read.
Shading drains the color and the contrast. Blurring needs Android 12 or newer, and the system drops it while battery saver is on.
Pauses DetoxDroid for a set time. You can start one from Quick Settings, the Assistant or a hardware button.
When the pause ends, DetoxDroid automatically resumes.
So pausing doesn\'t quietly become the habit.
Set DetoxDroid as your default assistant app to start a pause. (Assistant is often opened by long-pressing Home.)
Choose a hardware button to long-press for 2 seconds to pause DetoxDroid.
Press any hardware button on your phone
DetoxDroid must be running to assign a hardware button.
Show a foreground notification with a pause action. Requires notification permission.
Choose which features a pause turns off. Unchecked features keep running during a pause.
For when the feed won\'t end

How easily fast feed-scrolling triggers a break. \"Strict\" intervenes soonest. Endless feeds are always detected.

Nothing here runs away. Enjoy a few more minutes to yourself.

Make them wait, or lock them away
Makes selected apps wait before they open, and blocks or deactivates them once their daily time is up, launcher access and notifications included.
Set allowed daily screen time for these apps. After that, they are deactivated until the next day. (DetoxDroid must be running to track screen time.)
These apps make you wait before they open. Once you\'ve waited, an app opens right away until the screen turns off.
With 0 min of daily screen time the apps are locked right away, so there is nothing to wait for. Set some time first, or no limit.
Choose whether to block apps with a warning screen or fully deactivate them. Deactivate mode needs extra permissions.
You have used up your daily screen time for this app.
Take a break and come back tomorrow.
%1$s will be ready in a moment. Plenty of time to change your mind.
Protect selected DetoxDroid settings with a passphrase so they cannot be changed impulsively. Requires Device Admin.
Grant Device Admin to enable Commitment Password.

Enabling Commitment Password will:

• Lock selected settings
• Require your passphrase for changes
• Prevent stopping DetoxDroid while locked
• Allow 3 attempts, then a 5-minute cooldown
• Offer 24-hour recovery if forgotten

Only enable this if you stored your passphrase safely.

Continue?

Save this passphrase now. You need it to change protected settings:

%s

Write it down or store it in a secure place before continuing.
Enter your passphrase to unlock settings for this session.
Too many failed attempts. Try again in %s.
If you forgot your passphrase, start a 24-hour recovery timer. After it ends, you can reset the passphrase.\n\nSettings stay locked during recovery.
The 24-hour waiting period is complete. You can now reset your passphrase.
Enter your passphrase to disable commitment password.
Settings are locked. Enter passphrase to edit.

Stats get better the longer DetoxDroid runs. Scroll data only exists while it is active.
Nothing to manage, no feature is active
Combines scroll volume with scroll speed
Combines total scroll count with the rate per minute (using a sqrt weighting) so brief bursts cannot outrank sustained doom-scrolling. Higher = more doom-scrolling.
No judgement. Time is just easier to feel this way.
What\'s an hour of your time worth?
Tap to see what your screen time is worth
Nothing will be configured. You can set up every feature later on its own screen, or replay this setup from the About screen.

DetoxDroid helps you break autopilot habits: it can gray out distracting apps, interrupt endless scrolling and block apps once your daily budget is used up. The next steps set it up around how you actually use your phone.
Everything stays on your device. DetoxDroid is open source, has no ads and collects nothing.
To suggest which apps to tame, and a daily budget you might actually keep, DetoxDroid needs the system\'s \"usage access\". It also feeds your statistics. The data never leaves your phone.
Granted. Now we can suggest actual apps.
You can skip this. Then we go by app category instead.
Based on your usage and app categories, these are probably your biggest time sinks. Change the selection if that\'s off. The next steps act on whatever stays selected.
No suitable apps were found on this device. You can still pick apps for every feature later on.
Pick a starting point. Every detail can be changed later.
Interrupts endless scrolling in the selected apps with a break screen.
Gentle, plus grayscale for the selected apps once the daily budget is used up. Without color they pull a lot less.
Balanced, plus a hard block once the daily budget is spent. Grayscale warns you shortly before.
Your daily allowance for the selected apps before DetoxDroid steps in.
Suggested from your last 7 days of usage
Your setup needs the permissions below. Grant what you like. The rest you can pick up later on the feature screens.
Needed to show break screens and to block apps.
Status and reminders while a detox feature is active.
A special permission that lets DetoxDroid control the system\'s color filters.
Tap to grant. Shizuku or root was detected on your device.
Tap for a guided setup. Or leave it, we\'ll remind you on the home screen.
DetoxDroid\'s engine: the accessibility service detects which app is in the foreground and applies your rules. No data leaves your device.
Tap to open the accessibility settings and enable DetoxDroid there.
DetoxDroid is configured. App lists, schedules and budgets stay editable from the home screen.
Scroll breaks are ready, but need the \"display over other apps\" permission before they can appear.
Distracting apps get dull and blurry after %s of daily use. Real grayscale needs a one-time setup.
Apps blocked after %s of daily use
App blocking is ready, but needs the \"display over other apps\" permission to work.
DetoxDroid\'s accessibility service is not enabled yet. You can start it from the home screen.
No apps were selected, so nothing was configured. Explore the features from the home screen.
Finishing replaces the app lists and daily budgets of the affected features with this selection.
Grant the missing permissions to switch these on. Later works too, we\'ll remind you on the home screen.
Grayscale needs a special permission, once. Without a computer the easiest route is Shizuku, a free helper app. Takes about five minutes, and the permission survives reboots.
Your device appears to be rooted. You can skip Shizuku and grant the permission directly.
Get the free Shizuku app from Google Play.

Open Shizuku and follow \"Start via Wireless debugging\". If Developer options are not enabled yet: in the phone settings, find \"Build number\" (usually under About phone) and tap it seven times, then enable \"Wireless debugging\" in the Developer options. Shizuku walks you through the pairing.
After every reboot you have to start Shizuku again. The permission it granted stays, though.
Shizuku will ask for your confirmation in a dialog.
One tap and DetoxDroid grants itself the color-filter permission through Shizuku.
The permission is granted and grayscale is ready. If it was waiting from your setup, it is now active.
To use this feature, grant elevated permissions from a computer with ADB:

Shizuku is available. You can try granting permissions with it.
